key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C self-fluxing coatings show a clear process trade-off: lower barrel fill reduces friction and porosity, while higher O/C ratio and longer inter-shot delay improve wear resistance and hardness.
engineering_relevance: These results provide process windows for designing durable restorative and wear-protective coatings for machine components, where surface finish, hardness, and wear life must be balanced.
evidence_signal: Performance was evaluated through microstructure, roughness, hardness, friction, and wear tests, with the best wear rate reaching 0.000189 mm³/(N·m) and hardness up to 905.6 HV.
watch_item: Optimizing for low friction can increase wear, and higher filling levels may induce residual-stress-driven microcracking, so parameter tuning must be application-specific.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
